title: SPICA: Retrieving Scenarios for Pluralistic In-Context Alignment
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measures how effectively Large Language Models can be aligned with the values and preferences of different demographic groups, where one of the key distinctions between groups is based on their self-reported regular participation in religious activities.
findings: The SPICA framework, which uses group-informed metrics for in-context example retrieval, significantly improved alignment for groups defined by religious participation compared to a standard similarity-based approach. Groups with higher religious affinity ('-REL') saw a more marked improvement in retrieval quality. The framework also led to more equitable outcomes, where both religious and non-religious groups (in combination with political affiliation) preferred the aligned outputs, unlike the baseline where some groups preferred the unaligned outputs. This suggests SPICA is effective for aligning models to values that may diverge from a model's default, such as those held by certain religious or political groups.
